introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. Citizenship Education 1, 0562, JUNE 2026, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, duration one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed ORDINARY LEVEL - 0562 CITIZENSHIP EDUCATION 1. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question; if you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces. At the end of the examination the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet.

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is used to describe a situation where someone acquires citizenship by bearing the citizenship of his/her biological parents?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Citizenship by **descent** (the blood link) is acquired because one's biological parents are citizens of the country, wherever the child is born. Citizenship by birth depends on the place of birth, adoption is a legal procedure, and naturalisation is granted to a foreigner after an application.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Parents or adults who adopt a child or children and live with them are called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Foster parents** are adults who take in a child who is not their own, bring the child up and live with the child. Step parents are the new husband or wife of a child's biological parent, and "second parents" is not a standard term. "Non-biological parents" is a general description that also covers step parents, so it is less precise than foster parents.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mary is the daughter of my uncle, therefore, she is my...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The children of one's uncle or aunt are one's **cousins**. A sister has the same parents as I do, a niece is the daughter of my brother or sister, and a nephew is a boy (the son of my brother or sister).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An extensive area with people having similar language, culture and history is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **ethnic group** is a large community of people who share a common language, culture and history and who generally occupy a wide area. A clan is smaller and groups families that claim a common ancestor, a village is a small settlement, and "tribe" is usually used for a smaller or more traditional unit.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the letter linked to the most important form of family protection in Cameroon.

*Options as printed:* A) Payment of family allowance   B) HIV/AIDS Education   C) Marriage   D) Family planning
questions.corrige_markdown:
The family is protected by the State and by society in several ways. Family allowances paid through the social security system help parents to meet the cost of bringing up their children, which makes them the form of material protection most often cited. Marriage gives the family its legal basis, while HIV/AIDS education and family planning are health education measures. The printed question does not say what kind of protection is meant, so more than one option can be defended.

**Intended answer: A (Payment of family allowance).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which road users are restricted to the extreme right path of the carriage way?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Cameroon, where traffic keeps to the right, slow vehicles such as **bicycles** must keep to the extreme right of the carriageway so as not to obstruct faster vehicles. Pedestrians use the footpath or the verge, and cars and trucks use the lanes of the carriageway.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Once on the highway, we should all observe...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Every road user, whether driver, cyclist or pedestrian, must obey and observe **road signs** (signals and markings), because they regulate traffic and prevent accidents.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A school owned by the Baptist Mission is an example of a...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A school that belongs to a Christian mission or church is a **denominational** (confessional) school. A public school belongs to the State, a lay private school belongs to a private individual or company without a religious body behind it, and a vocational school is defined by the training it gives, not by its owner.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A student who habitually keeps away from school without justification is said to be guilty of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Truancy** is the habit of staying away from school without a valid reason. Indecency is improper dress or behaviour, and insubordination is refusal to obey authority.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the appropriate social distinction between a village and a town?

*Options as printed:* A) Villages have a fixed market day and towns have daily markets.   B) Villages have a high degree of solidarity and belief in tradition than towns.   C) Villages are smaller in size than towns.   D) Villages have a common economic activity and towns have multiple economic activities.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Villages and towns differ in several ways. A village is small, its people mostly share one main economic activity (usually farming), and social ties and tradition are strong. A town is larger, offers many different economic activities (trade, administration, industry, services) and its social life is more varied and less tied to tradition. The distinction most often given in civic education is the common economic activity of a village and the multiple activities of a town. Options B and D are both defensible, which is why the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Villages have a common economic activity and towns have multiple economic activities).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: rural and urban life in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: A pull factor that has caused many youths to move from villages to towns in Cameroon is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A pull factor is something that attracts people to a place. **Job opportunities** in towns attract young people. Natural disasters, poverty and hardship, and witchcraft are push factors, because they drive people away from the village.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The council performs all of the following functions except one. Identify the exception.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A council registers births, marriages and deaths (civil status), collects local taxes and fees, and issues building permits. **Councillors are elected** by the people, they are not appointed by the council, so appointing councillors is not a function of the council.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Each year millions of trees disappear from our forests due to man's activities. This is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Deforestation** is the destruction of forests by human activities such as farming, logging and bush fires. Reforestation is the planting of trees again, conservation is the protection of resources, and desertification is the spread of desert-like conditions.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the disease caused mostly by air pollution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Polluted air affects the lungs and the respiratory system, and **tuberculosis** is an air-borne disease of the lungs. Cholera and typhoid fever are spread by dirty water and food, and malaria is spread by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: To better protect the environment, household waste can be managed through...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Recycling** turns waste into new useful materials, reduces the quantity of rubbish and protects the environment. Burning pollutes the air, and dumping and burying waste can pollute the soil and water.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "He coordinates the activities of the Governor's office and assists the Governor in his absence". This refers to the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Region, the **Secretary General** of the Governor's office coordinates the activities of the services of the office and assists the Governor, including in his absence. A Senior Divisional Officer heads a Division, and a Chief of Protocol organises ceremonies and receptions.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An important duty of the Governor is to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Governor is the representative of the Head of State and of the Government in the Region, so one of his duties is to represent the President at official ceremonies. Local administrators are appointed at a higher level, council decisions are carried out by the council executive (the mayor), and sentencing criminals belongs to the courts.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: represent the Head of State during national ceremonies.
order the imprisonment of persons guilty of crimes.

questions.enonce_markdown: In which Ministerial department do Senior Divisional Officers in Cameroon fall?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Governors, Senior Divisional Officers and Divisional Officers are the officers of the territorial administration, which is under the **Ministry of Territorial Administration**.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reforms.
Ministry of Decentralisation and Local Government.
Ministry of Economy, Planning, and Regional Development.

questions.enonce_markdown: The major difference between Central and External Administrative Services is that...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Central services are in the Ministries at the seat of government, where policies are designed. **External services** are the offices of the Ministries in the Regions, Divisions and Sub-divisions, and they work in the field, in direct contact with the population. The other statements are either false or describe a minor point.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the External Services deal directly with the population.
the Central Administration cannot take decisions which directly affect the population.
their headquarters are not found in the same town.
both services organise separate tours to meet the population.

questions.enonce_markdown: Mr. Bate gave a job to Mrs. Ebamau simply because they are from the same village, instead of Mrs. Jam who is more qualified. Mr. Bate is therefore guilty of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Favouring someone because of the village or ethnic group they come from, instead of merit, is **tribalism**. Bigotry is intolerance of other beliefs, corruption involves a bribe or an abuse of office for gain, and fraud is dishonest deception for gain.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation where persons are devoted to their beliefs and natural dispositions and are intolerant towards those with different beliefs and natural dispositions is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Bigotry** is strong, stubborn attachment to one's own beliefs and intolerance of people who think or behave differently. Tribalism and sectionalism favour one's own group, and nepotism favours relatives.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most commonly consumed drug in Cameroon is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Alcohol** is the most widely consumed drug in Cameroon, because it is legal, cheap, easy to find and socially accepted in many settings. Tobacco, cannabis and tramadol are also abused but by fewer people.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A case of examination malpractice punishable by imprisonment is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Impersonation**, where a person sits an examination in the name of another candidate, is a serious offence which can lead to a prison sentence as well as exclusion from the examination. Lateness and noise making are breaches of discipline, and collusion (cheating together) is normally punished by cancellation of results or exclusion.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Social re-integration centres in Cameroon are intended to...

*Options as printed:* A) rebuild the character of delinquents.   B) re-educate school drop-outs.   C) restore the dignity of former prostitutes.   D) recover the joy of divorced couples.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Social re-integration (rehabilitation) centres receive young people in difficulty, such as juvenile delinquents, and help them to change their behaviour and return to normal life in society. They can also help other vulnerable persons, so options A and C are both defensible, while B (school drop-outs) belongs to vocational and education services and D (divorced couples) has no link with these centres. The intended answer is to rebuild the character of delinquents.

**Intended answer: A (rebuild the character of delinquents).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Structure created by the Cameroon Government to fight corruption in the country is the ...

*Options as printed:* A) Penal code.   B) Constitution.   C) National Program on Governance.   D) Audit Bench of the Supreme Court.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The body usually named as the structure set up by the Government to fight corruption is the National Anti-Corruption Commission (CONAC), which is not among the printed options. The National Programme on Governance is a government programme that includes the fight against corruption among its aims, the Audit Bench of the Supreme Court controls public accounts, and the Penal Code and the Constitution are legal texts, not structures. Because the expected institution is missing, the question is left open.

**Intended answer: the National Anti-Corruption Commission (CONAC), which is not printed among the options.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most outstanding mark of a referendum is that...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a referendum the people are asked a single question about a proposal (for example a change in the law) and answer with **"Yes" or "No"**. They do not choose between candidates. A referendum is not limited to councillors, is not tied to a fixed five-year cycle, and the voting age is the general voting age.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: it is organised once in five years.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which national symbol shows the authenticity and originality of government documents?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **Seal** of the Republic is stamped on official documents to show that they are genuine and come from the State. The motto expresses an ideal, the flag represents the nation, and the coat of arms is the emblem of the State.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Important years in Cameroon's Constitutional History are...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The main dates are 1961 (federal constitution after the reunification), 1972 (the federation replaced by a unitary State), 1984 (the country took the name Republic of Cameroon) and 1996 (a revised constitution introducing decentralisation and the Senate). Only option A lists exactly these dates.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which constitution in Cameroon created the Senate as the Upper House of the National Assembly?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Senate is the upper house of Parliament. It was provided for by the **1996 Constitution**, which established a Parliament of two houses, the National Assembly and the Senate. The earlier constitutions had a single legislative assembly.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are arms of government in Cameroon EXCEPT the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three arms of government are the **Legislature** (makes laws), the **Executive** (carries out laws) and the **Judiciary** (interprets laws and settles disputes). The Presidency is an office within the Executive, not a separate arm.

**Answer: C.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: The state institution that certifies the regularity of Presidential and Parliamentary elections in Cameroon falls under the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The institution that supervises the regularity of Presidential and parliamentary elections and settles election disputes is the Constitutional Council, which acts as a court. In civic education textbooks it is placed in the judicial arm, so the answer is the **Judiciary**. The Executive and the Legislature are interested parties in the election and cannot check it.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Peter is sentenced to a four-year imprisonment term but serves only three, due to Presidential clemency. This illustrates the relationship between...

*Options as printed:* A) Judiciary and Executive.   B) Judiciary and Legislature.   C) Legislature and Executive.   D) Executive and Judiciary.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The court (the **Judiciary**) passed the sentence, and the Head of State (the **Executive**) reduced it by an act of clemency. This shows the link between the Judiciary and the Executive. The Legislature is not involved.

**Intended answer: A (Judiciary and Executive).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: The electoral process in Cameroon begins with the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
No one can vote without being on the electoral register, so the first step is the **registration of potential voters**. The other steps (registration of candidates, campaigns, convening of voters, voting) follow.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: convening of voters to the polls.

questions.enonce_markdown: There are about 10 million potential voters in Cameroon, but just over 1 million turned out to vote in the last Legislative and Municipal elections. This is an example of....
questions.corrige_markdown:
When most registered or potential voters do not go to the polls, this shows a lack of interest in voting, called **voter apathy**. Disenfranchisement means that people are prevented from voting, and vote rigging is cheating in the counting of votes.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A consequence of electoral malpractice in Cameroon is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Electoral malpractice means cheating in the electoral process. Its consequence is the **violation of the will of the electorate**, since the result no longer reflects the choice of the voters. The other three options are themselves forms of malpractice, not consequences.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: violation of the will of the electorate.
polling stations are found in private homes.
the election calendar is not made public.

questions.enonce_markdown: A written and signed instruction from an account holder to his bank authorizing payment from his account to the specified name is referred to as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **cheque** is a written, signed order from the account holder to the bank to pay a stated sum to the named person. A bank statement or account statement is a record of the transactions on an account sent by the bank, and a voucher is a document that proves a payment or entitles the holder to goods or services.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is distribution considered as part of the production process?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Production is not complete until the goods and services reach the people who need them. Distribution (transport, wholesale and retail) **makes goods and services available to the final consumer**, which adds place utility to them. This is why it is part of the production process.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It transports goods from place to place.
It makes goods and services available to the final consumer
It encourages the provision of transport means
It links the consumer with the buyer

questions.enonce_markdown:
Economic growth can only lead to economic development if a country's...

*Options as printed:* A) natural resources are sufficient.   B) tax policies are favourable.   C) imports outweigh exports.   D) loan refund is high.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth is an increase in the total output of a country. It leads to economic development only when the benefits are shared and improve the living conditions of the people (education, health, housing, jobs). None of the printed options states this condition clearly. Sufficient natural resources and favourable tax policies can both help, while imports greater than exports and high loan repayments weaken an economy. The question is therefore left open.

**Intended answer: the benefits of growth must be shared and improve the living standards of the people (no printed option states this exactly).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are internal sources of government revenue EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Internal sources are those found inside the country: rents on public property, the sale of State enterprises (privatisation) and money collected inside the country. **Loans from the African Development Bank** come from outside the country, so they are an external source.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: loans from the African Development Bank.

questions.enonce_markdown: An outstanding effect of tax evasion is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax evasion means refusing to pay taxes that are due. The State then collects less money, so there is a **fall in government revenue**, and it has less to spend on public services. Imprisonment is a possible punishment, not the main effect.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Human Rights are universal because they are applicable...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Human rights are universal because they belong to every human being **everywhere**, whatever the person's nationality, sex, race, religion or social position. They are therefore applicable to everybody.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Child labour is most likely to violate the child's right to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A child who works long hours has no time or energy to go to school, so child labour mostly violates the child's right to **education**. It can also harm health, but the effect on schooling is the most direct.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One important role of the National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms is to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms promotes and protects human rights, receives complaints and **investigates violations of human rights**. Punishing offenders is the work of the courts, making laws is the work of Parliament, and elections are organised by the electoral body.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: investigate the violation of human rights.
punish those guilty of human rights violations.
pass laws on protection of human rights.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which international body has the powers to prosecute people who have committed crimes against humanity?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **International Criminal Court** (ICC) tries individuals accused of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. The International Court of Justice settles disputes between States, not between individuals.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An aspect of good governance where the governing class freely and regularly informs the governed about their actions is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Transparency** means that leaders act openly and give the people clear and regular information on what they do. Accountability means being answerable for one's actions and accepting the consequences, participation means involving the people in decisions, and efficiency means using resources well.

**Answer: A.**
themes: good governance and the rule of law

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is not a material consequence of war?

*Options as printed:* A) Loss of lives   B) Destruction of property   C) Wastage of economic resources   D) Mutual suspicion and hatred.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Destruction of property and wastage of economic resources are material (physical and economic) losses. Mutual suspicion and hatred is a psychological and social consequence, so it is not material. However, loss of lives is a human consequence and is not material either, so two options fit the question. It is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Mutual suspicion and hatred).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The statement, 'women are supposed to cook and do house work' is an expression of gender...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **gender stereotype** is a fixed and generalised idea about the roles that men and women are supposed to play. Saying that women should cook and do housework is such an idea. Discrimination and inequality would be unequal treatment in practice.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Minority groups in Cameroon could better defend their rights through...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Minority groups can defend their rights peacefully and lawfully by **forming associations** which speak for them and put their case to the authorities. Violent protests break the law, and constitutional revision and the creation of administrative units are decisions taken by the State, not by the minorities.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a manifestation of terrorism?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Terrorism is the use of violence and fear to force a government or a society to accept demands, and it is often driven by **religious fanaticism**, which is extreme and intolerant attachment to a belief. Open criticism and strike action are lawful ways of expressing disagreement, and violation of the law is too general to be specific to terrorism.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One undesirable effect of refugees to the host country is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A large influx of refugees puts pressure on food, housing, health services, schools and jobs, and it can **slow down economic development** of the host area. A reduction in population and a fall in labour supply are the opposite of what happens, and diversification of economic activities is a benefit.

**Answer: D.**
